Adding @triton.autotune explores the optimal combination automatically, also addressing the 20% partial-wave tail by finding a grid shape that minimizes partial waves.

strategy_title: Larger BLOCK_K with smaller BLOCK_N worsens register pressure
strategy_description: Changing tile dimensions from BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32 to BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=32/BLOCK_K=64 increased registers per thread from 96 to 128, which cut theoretical occupancy from 31.25% to 12.5% (Block Limit Shared Mem dropped from 5 to 2). Despite the intent to reduce wasted computation on the narrow N dimension, the larger BLOCK_K dramatically increased register pressure, causing compute throughput to fall from 76.6% to 59.2% and duration to increase by 31%. When a kernel is already register-limited, increasing BLOCK_K (which expands the accumulator tile and loop-carried state) will raise register count further and compound the occupancy problem rather than solve it.
slow_pseudocode:
BLOCK_M = 64
BLOCK_N = 64
BLOCK_K = 32
# registers_per_thread = 96, theoretical_occupancy = 31.25%
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
    a = load(A[m_tile, k_tile])  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]
    b = load(B[k_tile, n_tile])  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
    acc += dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:

BLOCK_M = 128
BLOCK_N = 32
BLOCK_K = 64
# registers_per_thread = 128, theoretical_occupancy = 12.5%

    a = load(A[m_tile, k_tile])  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]
    b = load(B[k_tile, n_tile])  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
    acc += dot(a, b)
applicable_when: Never: this specific combination of larger BLOCK_K + larger BLOCK_M when the kernel is already register-limited is an anti-pattern. Avoid when registers_per_thread >= 80 and Block Limit Registers is already the binding occupancy constraint.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already register-limited (registers_per_thread > 80, Block Limit Registers < Block Limit Warps). Increasing BLOCK_K or BLOCK_M in this regime will increase register count further, crush occupancy, and increase latency even if arithmetic intensity improves on paper.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_K controls the inner reduction tile size. Larger BLOCK_K means more accumulator registers are live simultaneously across the dot product loop, directly increasing register pressure. This is distinct from num_stages (software pipelining), which also increases register usage but for prefetch buffers. Both effects compound when BLOCK_M is also increased.
